chapter: Luck, tricks and the Bourbon Street job
title: The flaxseed trick to draw crowds from rival country bands
summary: Valentine tells how he told a host to sprinkle flaxseed along the road so that people followed it to his dance, closing down rival bands such as Clabon Williams'.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: You were telling about, you know when it was a little bit slow getting started there this winter, how one time that they, you said you could get the crowd coming there, what was that you used there? Oh yeah, you were talking about the bus?

Flaxseed, what was it? Flaxseed? Flaxseed, yeah you see, I tell her, we was playing in the country, you see. We used to go to play in the country, or we used to go, you see like holidays coming there now? Yeah. We would miss playing all them holidays in the country, you see. So the boy we was playing for, this boy Sero, you know he came from that St. James Parish, you know. Oh yeah. Well this boy, him and this boy grew up together, see. Well every time we'd have a dance ball we'd high in the play. So we'd go, we'd go out there. Well most of the time we'd go, make no difference, it wouldn't be no, it could be any other night, Saturday night or Sunday night, it wouldn't make no difference. Most of the time we'd go to always have a dance elsewhere, you know maybe. The dance wouldn't be that close, it'd be a couple of miles apart, you see. So this man he'd be worried you know. You see well, and the band they used to have, in them days, a lot of pretty good bands, you see, there was good bands, you see. Man sometimes Cleven Williams would be playing them dances there, different bands, good bands, you know what I mean. So I used to tell him all the time, we used to tell him all the time, man, say we ain't worried about them bands, because we going to close them up. Just like that. He said, how you know? I said, man we going to close them people up. So to make him, you know what I mean, to make him convinced, I said, you know what you do? I said, you go to the drugstore and get your butter, maybe a couple of pounds of flaxseed, just sprinkle it all up and down from the dance hall, from them people's dance hall to your
I said, that's how boys feed. You see Mr. Bill, you take for instance, look, you take a boy at a chicken, man you could put something, corn.
Yeah they'll follow that down there, you know.

Tilt it in. Well that's how people do. You see, well so, well he did that. And sure man for nine o'clock that place was closed up. Closed up. Sure, and we used to close them all down, Mr. Bill. That didn't matter. We used to, every time we go, I don't care what band we be playing out there, we close them people down flat. Clabon Williams, band from here.
I'm telling. I remember you told once, you sent some, was it some musician out to get some flaxseed? Yeah, John Smith. And they got the, you know.
